# Night photography of the Milky Way

Golden hour light is warm and low, which softens shadows and adds texture to faces and buildings. A polarising filter removes glare from water and deepens a blue sky. A fast prime lens gathers more light and forces you to move your feet to frame the shot. RAW files keep more highlight and shadow detail than JPEG, which gives room in editing.

## Open questions

Leading lines pull the eye through the frame toward the subject. For the Milky Way use a wide lens, the widest aperture and an exposure under twenty seconds to avoid trails. A polarising filter removes glare from water and deepens a blue sky.

A fast prime lens gathers more light and forces you to move your feet to frame the shot. Back button focus separates focusing from the shutter and helps with moving subjects.
